questions: Are the numbers on each die's faces guaranteed to be distinct, or can a die have repeated values among its faces?
When rolling a die, does each face have equal probability of appearing, i.e., are the dice fair?
Should the probability be output as a reduced fraction, a decimal, or in some specific format (e.g., with a certain precision)?
If the optimal probability is zero (no common numbers between any pair), what should be printed (e.g., 0, 0.0, 0/1)?
Are the dice considered ordered when choosing two dice (i.e., is choosing die i and die j the same as choosing die j and die i)?
Can the same die be chosen twice (i.e., rolling the same die two times), or must the two dice be distinct?
What is the required tolerance for floating‑point answers if a decimal representation is used (e.g., absolute or relative error)?
Are there any limits on the values of K_i beyond the given sum constraint (e.g., can K_i be zero)?

inline_prompts: There are N dice. The i-th die has K_i faces, with the numbers A_{i,1}, A_{i,2}, \ldots, A_{i,K_i} written on them. When you roll this die, each face appears. You choose two dice from the N dice and roll them. Determine the maximum probability that the two dice show the same number, when the dice are chosen optimally. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K_1 A_{1,1} A_{1,2} \dots A_{1,K_1} \vdots K_N A_{N,1} A_{N,2} \dots A_{N,K_N} Output Print the answer. Constraints - 2 \leq N \leq 100 - 1 \leq K_i - K_1 + K_2 + \dots + K_N \leq 10^5 - 1 \leq A_{i,j} \leq 10^5 - All input values are integers. Not addressed by the given clarifications.
